t: Not later than 180 days after the date of the enactment of this Act, the Secretary of Agriculture shall issue a final rule based on the proposed rule entitled “National Organic Program; Origin of Livestock,” published in the Federal Register on April 28, 2015 (80 Fed. Reg. 23455):  Provided, That the final rule shall incorporate public comments submitted in response to the proposed rule.

fable.w: The section requires the Secretary to issue a final rule and to incorporate public comments submitted on the proposed rule, so input from outside the federal government must shape a federal decision. The tempting contrary reading is that the comment period is already over and this is only a deadline directive. That fails because the definition counts required rulemaking as participation, and the text expressly makes the public's comments part of the final rule.
fable.s: the Secretary of Agriculture shall issue a final rule based on the proposed rule entitled “National Organic Program; Origin of Livestock,” published in the Federal Register on April 28, 2015 (80 Fed. Reg. 23455):  Provided, That the final rule shall incorporate public comments submitted in response to the proposed rule.

qwen_block.w: The section explicitly requires the Secretary of Agriculture to incorporate public comments into the final rule. Public comments are submitted by people outside the federal government, and their inclusion in the decision-making process constitutes participation as defined.
qwen_block.s: Provided, That the final rule shall incorporate public comments submitted in response to the proposed rule.

opus.w: The section requires rulemaking, which counts as participation under the DEFINITION. It also expressly requires the final federal decision to incorporate public comments, so input from outsiders must shape the rule. The comments were submitted in the past, but the decision they feed into is still to come, so this is unlike Example 5's purely historical agreement.
opus.s: the Secretary of Agriculture shall issue a final rule based on the proposed rule entitled “National Organic Program; Origin of Livestock,” published in the Federal Register on April 28, 2015 (80 Fed. Reg. 23455):  Provided, That the final rule shall incorporate public comments submitted in response to the proposed rule.
opus.b: **Tempting wrong reading:** The comment period on the 2015 proposed rule has already closed. Read alongside Example 5, which involved only a past agreement, this could look like there is no outside participation left to happen. That reading fails because the federal decision, the final rule, has not been made yet. The statute requires that rule to "incorporate public comments," so the public's input must shape a decision still to come. Separately, the DEFINITION treats any requirement to make a rule as "Yes."

qwen_chat.w: The section requires the Secretary of Agriculture to issue a final rule that incorporates public comments. Public comments are submissions from the general public (outside the federal government) regarding a federal regulatory decision. The definition explicitly lists 'requiring a public comment period' as a form of participation. By mandating the incorporation of these comments, the statute ensures outside parties participate in the decision.
qwen_chat.s: Provided, That the final rule shall incorporate public comments submitted in response to the proposed rule.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that this is just an administrative directive to finalize a rule and that the comment period already happened, so no *new* participation is required here. However, the definition explicitly states that "requiring a public comment period" is a form of participation. By mandating that the final rule *incorporate* public comments, the statute ensures that the public's input (an outside party) is part of the federal decision-making process. The requirement to consider and incorporate these comments is the participatory element.
